FINDING: the docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:255 line anomaly is explained — the reporting path is exonerated.

Evidence (git archaeology, 2026-07-26):
- Test files are .exs: ExUnit compiles them from disk at run time, no beam cache. An artifact event's line therefore always reflects the on-disk file AT RUN START, not any stale compile.
- The cz0 session's branch (specled_-cz0/spec-honesty, still alive) shows seven micro-commits touching this exact file. Across them, test 'a fabricated, unmarked finding code IS flagged' sat at lines 182, 231, 242, 250, 256, 266, 268 — the file churned +/-6 lines around 255 all session.
- 4c9aa6864 has that test at 250 and the 'evidence/*' test head at 256/257 with 255 blank — precisely the state the original comment describes inspecting. Adjacent states (833a83fe, 966464d9) have an @tag at 255 and a test decl at 256.
- Conclusion: the failing run executed an uncommitted working state where a test declaration sat at 255; the 'line 255 is blank' inspection read a different (shifted) state. 'No edits between runs' was wrong at file granularity — the session was editing this exact file between spec.check invocations.

Impact on this ticket's scope: the descriptor-id change is MORE valuable, not less — a test NAME is shift-proof where a line number is not; this failure mode (report generated against tree state A, investigated against tree state B) will recur in any session that edits between gate runs. Two scope additions worth making: (1) preserve the attribution artifact JSONL alongside the SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR capture on failure (run_merged_command's `after File.rm(artifact_path)` currently destroys it — it is primary evidence); (2) have the forensic capture record run-time provenance (git rev-parse HEAD + dirty-file list) so report-vs-inspection tree skew is detectable next time.

Still genuinely open: WHY a doc-integrity lint test failed once-in-five under load (the assertions near every candidate line are pure-constant), and the verifier_test.exs:1452 site. Both need the armed forensics; neither needs the reporting path investigated further.

I wrote nothing to the worktree. Evidence: the ticket and all fifteen comments; the
two spec files and the ADR; `git diff ca703617..HEAD`, `git diff c9b8fea1..e21dfe8e`
(what the merge brought in), `git show ca703617:` and `git show c9b8fea1:` for the
conflicted files; `git show 7b3d97cd:` for the comment-stripped comparison; and
lib/specled_ex/{verifier.ex,tagged_tests/attribution.ex}, test/test_helper.exs,
scripts/check_specs.sh, Makefile, .gitignore, .spec/AGENTS.md read at HEAD.

I found an ELEVENTH false claim. It is advisory, not blocking, and I say why below.

Reasoning:

(1) THE THREE `must` REQUIREMENTS — traced, not read off the coverage table.

specled.tagged_tests.descriptors_self_identify. attribution_test.exs:184 asserts
the WHOLE return map by `==` against the literal
`%{"req.a" => {:failed, ["test/docs_lint.exs:255 (DocsLintTest.test a code IS flagged)"]}}`,
so dropping either half fails on string inequality; :207 does the same for the
in_flight half via a started-only event. :214 pins all four {location, id}
nil-combinations including the `"unknown test"` placeholder; :233 pins the
`id != ""` and `is_integer(line)` guards that attribution.ex:157-173 implement —
and those two guards are the ones a naive rewrite drops, so the test is not
decorative. These call the PUBLIC `Attribution.attribute/2`, which is the same
entry point verifier.ex consumes, not the private `descriptor/1`; pure maps in,
no mocks, no seam. The PRODUCTION format is pinned separately at
verifier_test.exs:1564, where a real shell shim drives a merged run to timeout
and the finding must contain the exact
`"timed out while running test/alpha_test.exs:42 (AlphaTest.hang)"`. That is the
requirement's own subject matter, not an adjacent one.

specled.verify.command_capture_run_provenance. :2017 — real `init_git_repo` +
commit + one uncommitted file, asserting the exact HEAD sha, `git_dirty: 1
path(s)`, the named dirty file, and `refute captured =~ "and 0 more"`. :2072 —
unborn branch, asserting the literal `git_head: unavailable (no resolvable git
HEAD at the verification root)` AND `refute captured =~ "git_dirty:"`, which is
what distinguishes "present and answered" from "omitted", the distinction the
requirement's last clause is about. :2115 — clean tree asserted as
`git_dirty: none (clean work tree)`, then 60 dirty paths asserted down to
`git_dirty: 60 path(s)`, `"... and 10 more"`, and a COUNT of exactly 50 lines
matching `~r/^  \?\? dirty_\d+\.txt$/`. The truncation clause the round-1 verifier
found uncovered is genuinely exercised; the count assertion is what makes it a
bound test rather than a happy path.

specled.tagged_tests.failed_run_preserves_attribution_artifact. :2174 asserts the
artifact lands at `Path.rootname(capture_path) <> ".attribution.jsonl"` and still
carries the failed event id, its state, and `suite_finished` — the basename
correlation and the content survival are both load-bearing. The NEGATIVE is at
:1479 inside the artifact-naming test: `Path.wildcard(Path.join(capture_dir, "*")) == []`
on a GREEN merged run, so "writes nothing on success" is pinned. :2215 proves the
merged path survives an unwritable capture dir with findings and claim strengths
intact and warns once. The residual — the artifact write specifically failing —
is not tested and is disclosed; see (5).

(2) SEAM WALK, every hop read at HEAD. run_merged_command/5 is the only site
passing `preserve_artifact:` (verifier.ex:2178-2184); run_command/4 forwards it at
:2383 via `Keyword.get(opts, :preserve_artifact)` into preserve_failed_output/4
(:2416); preserve_artifact/2 is invoked at :2433 inside that function's try body,
whose single `rescue e in File.Error` sits below it. The generic command path
passes no opts and lands on the `preserve_artifact(nil, _capture_path), do: :ok`
clause. I grepped lib/ and test/ for every `SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR` reference
to confirm there is no second production consumer. Production path connected. No
INTEGRATION_REGRESSION_LATENT.

(3) ITEM (a) — THE ROUND-2 BLOCKING FINDING IS GENUINELY FIXED, and I verified the
line numbers and directions by reading rather than accepting them.

verifier_test.exs:2223-2237 now reads: raising at the head of preserve_artifact/2's
non-nil clause over the WHOLE module leaves this test green while two others redden
— `"a failing merged run files its attribution artifact beside the output capture"`
(:2174, above) and `"a shared-fate timeout finding echoes the ExUnit seed and its
capture records timed_out"` (:1764).

- :2174 IS that test's declaration line and IS above the comment (which sits inside
  the test declared at :2215). The stated direction is correct. The round-2 defect
  ("below", pointing at :2269, the generic sibling the same paragraph excludes) is
  gone.
- :1764 IS that test's declaration line. I checked whether it actually reaches
  preserve_artifact/2 rather than taking the implementer's word: it arms
  SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR at :1767 to a writable dir under the fixture root,
  drives `run_two_subject_merged` (so artifact_path is non-nil), and its shim
  `sleep 5`s into a timeout, so preserve_failed_output/4's
  `result.timed_out or result.exit_code != 0` guard fires, mkdir_p! and the log
  write succeed, and preserve_artifact/2 is called. A raise at the HEAD of the
  non-nil clause fires before `File.read`, which is why it reddens even though that
  shim never writes an artifact — and stating the probe's position is exactly what
  round 2 demanded, because the answer turns on it.
- I re-derived the count independently instead of accepting "two". Repo-wide, only
  verifier_test.exs arms the variable (test_helper.exs deletes it before
  ExUnit.start/0; no other test file mentions it). Within that module the arming
  sites are :1480, :1767, :1975, :2038, :2081, :2137/:2149, :2177, :2248, :2272/:2300.
  Of those, the merged ones are :1480 (green run — guard false, not reached),
  :1767 (reached), :2177 (reached), :2248 (mkdir_p! raises first — not reached);
  the rest drive generic commands and pass nil. Exactly two. "Only" is now true and
  the module scope stated is sufficient.

(4) ITEM (c) — THE MERGE. I judge it acceptable to approve over without a verifier
pass, and I checked the resolution myself.

- The conflict resolution is CORRECT. main renamed the reference (release 0.9.6
  marked specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names `status: superseded`,
  `superseded_by: specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names_reach` — I read the
  frontmatter); this branch had appended gate_failure_forensics. HEAD's
  tagged_tests_verification.spec.md `decisions:` list carries
  `cross_vm_temp_names_reach` + `gate_failure_forensics` and no longer carries the
  superseded id. The same one-line rename applied to verification.spec.md, resolved
  identically. Those two files are the ENTIRE intersection of "changed by the
  branch" and "changed by main" — I computed both sides and intersected them — so
  there was no other resolution to get wrong.
- .spec/realization_hashes.json was NOT regenerated. It is byte-identical to BOTH
  parents (`git diff ca703617..HEAD` and `git diff c9b8fea1..HEAD` on that path are
  both empty), i.e. unchanged since 402f4a27 on either side. The rule in
  .claude/rules/specled.md is respected.
- No branch lib/ or test/ file was touched by the merge. I confirmed
  test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs and test/test_helper.exs are byte-identical to
  7b3d97cd once comments and blank lines are stripped, so every mutation result and
  every requirement-coverage line from the 7b3d97cd-era records carries forward
  without re-derivation.
- What that leaves unverified is main's own lib changes interacting with this
  branch's — and the implementer's full-suite run (1272 tests, 0 failures) plus
  `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` = pass covers exactly that surface. A verifier
  round would re-run the same commands over a tree whose td7 content is provably
  unchanged. Not worth a bounce. The one residual is that bare `mix spec.check` has
  not been run at HEAD — but no VERIFY record on this ticket ever ran it, by design;
  it belongs to the merge gate / PR CI. Advisory A4.

(5) ITEM (f) — MUTATION (g), CORRECTLY DEFERRED, and the missing follow-up is
advisory not blocking. The code is right: I read it, and preserve_artifact/2 is
called inside preserve_failed_output/4's try body under its single
`rescue e in File.Error`, which is literally what the requirement demands. What no
test pins is that a FUTURE edit cannot move it under a parallel silent rescue. Two
independent reviewers reached the same conclusion for the same reason, and I agree
with the shape of the fix they proposed: "not a parallel one of its own... One
guard, one contract, one proof" is a constraint on source structure, not an
observable outcome, and the honest remedy is to trim the `must` to its observable
content — not to demand a test. Doing that spec surgery now, unverified, on a
branch that has already produced eleven prose defects, is worse than tracking it.
The follow-up ticket has not been created; that is a loose end to close at delivery,
not a reason to stop the pipeline. Advisory A3.

(6) MECHANICAL SCOPE, re-derived from the diff by hand.
`git diff --numstat ca703617..HEAD` sums to 16 files, 856 insertions, 18 deletions.
13 files map to td7 deliverables: attribution.ex + verifier.ex + their two test
files (changes 1-3); .claude/settings.json + Makefile + scripts/check_specs.sh +
.gitignore (change 4); test/test_helper.exs (round-2 critic A0); verification.spec.md
+ tagged_tests_verification.spec.md + the ADR + .spec/AGENTS.md (recorded policy).
3 belong to n5s (coverage_capture.spec.md 25/1, store.ex 12/1, store_test.exs 38/1
= 75 insertions), leaving 781 insertions and 15 deletions for td7. mix.exs and
mix.lock are untouched by this branch (main's merge brought its own mix.exs change,
correctly attributed to 0.9.6, which is why the old-base diff would have misled).
Nothing unexplained.

(7) INTENT-LEVEL. No new dependency. The capture stays opt-in behind
SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR — no library default writes to a consuming project's
filesystem — and only repo-owned gate wrappers arm it, matching the ADR's stated
alternative-rejection. The GREEN-run negative at :1479 is what keeps that honest.
No detection-evasion, no behavior-changing default. No intent violation found.

(8) ITEM (g) — n5s CO-TENANCY: ACCEPTABLE. The 3 files are disjoint from td7's; the
spec delta adds its own requirement ids (write_v2_argument_error_contract plus a
clause on envelope_meta) touching no td7 subject; the bundling was the user's
explicit call and n5s is separately cold-verified. Not re-audited.

(9) THE ELEVENTH FALSE CLAIM — FOUND, and it is in one of the five advisory
REPLACEMENTS from item (b), which is exactly where item (b) told me to look.

.spec/AGENTS.md:34-38 (key clause at :36), the replacement for the
"unconditionally" overstatement, introduced by c9b8fea1 — the commit whose message
is "fix the tenth false claim, in the anti-false-claim commit":

  "`make check` and `scripts/check_specs.sh` arm `SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR` at
   `tmp/specled-command-output` (gitignored) whenever it is unset — note that
   presetting it to the empty string defeats BOTH, since `make`'s `?=` treats
   empty as set and the verifier's own guard then ignores it."

"both" is false for scripts/check_specs.sh, and the stated reason does not even
reach it. That script uses `${SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR:-$ROOT/tmp/specled-command-output}`
(scripts/check_specs.sh:14). POSIX `:-` substitutes when the parameter is unset OR
NULL, so an empty preset re-arms it to the default. Only the Makefile's `?=` treats
an empty environment value as set. This is not my inference against the record —
this ticket's own DELTA VERIFY (2026-07-27T01:26:27Z) MEASURED both halves and wrote
the correct version: "check_specs.sh's `:-` treats empty as unset and re-arms, while
the Makefile's `?=` treats an empty env value as SET". The replacement prose inverted
one half of a finding already on the ticket, and it did so in the same conjunctive
"both are required / defeats both" shape as the Makefile falsehood the round-2 audit
caught. It also undercuts the very next paragraph, which recommends
`bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh` as the robust agent-facing path — the one the
sentence wrongly says is defeated.

Why ADVISORY and not BLOCKING, stated plainly since the budget matters. This claim
cannot produce a wrong gate outcome. It describes a pathological input nobody
supplies, it does not substitute for a missing test (which is what made the round-2
finding blocking), and it errs in the direction of claiming a hazard broader than
reality — the same class this ticket's DELTA VERIFY already graded advisory when it
found the subdirectory-scattering claim, with the reasoning "cannot cause a wrong
gate outcome, only a wasted investigation." A one-clause overreach in a doc
parenthetical is prose to tidy, and I was told not to bounce to tidy prose. It
should be corrected, and it should be corrected as a two-word edit
("defeats `make check`") rather than as a round.

(10) THE OTHER FOUR REPLACEMENTS FROM ITEM (b) — judged as claims.
- test_helper.exs:16 referent: "Measured on test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs alone
  (not the whole suite) at seeds 0, 1 and 424242: 9, 10 and 4 files." TRUE at HEAD.
  I counted the `System.delete_env("SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR")` sites in
  verifier_test.exs myself — 9 (lines 1481, 1795, 2012, 2067, 2110, 2169, 2210,
  2264, 2327) — which is the cleanup count the 9/10/4 figures were measured against
  at 7b3d97cd, and the file's code is byte-identical to 7b3d97cd. Referent fixed,
  figures still true.
- verifier.ex "reachable only through a filesystem state the first has already
  excluded": REPLACED and the specific overstatement retired — the new text
  concedes such states exist ("a disk filling between the two writes, or a race at
  the artifact path"). Partially resolved; see A2.
- verifier.ex git/2 rescue causes: TRUE and honestly framed. It names ErlangError
  :enoent as the one cause known to occur, records the measurement that a
  non-existent `:cd` returns {"", 2} rather than raising, and says ArgumentError and
  File.Error are "belt and braces, not because they are expected." `root` is a
  binary on every path into run_provenance/1 — I traced it from run_command/4.
- verifier.ex orphaned line break: fixed. The old text broke after "rather than",
  stranding "# costing the caller its forensic log." on its own line; at :2514-2515
  the same sentence now wraps at the fill column like ordinary prose.

(11) I ALSO CHECKED, and found true: the :2004-2010 comment's "their own tests
below" (the three provenance tests at :2017/:2072/:2115 are below the test at
:1972); "this arm fires on EVERY machine" for the unborn-branch test (rev-parse
HEAD on an unborn branch fails regardless of TMPDIR); "would leak this VM-global
into every later test in this sync module" (the module is `async: false`,
verifier_test.exs:3); "both capture dirs are committed as ignored" (the fixture
writes `capture/\nclean_capture/\n` to .gitignore and commits before dirtying);
the .gitignore comment's account of `**/` anchoring and of why no gate path runs
outside the repo root; the ADR's "at most two `git` invocations... only on the
failure path"; and that attribution.ex's edit lands at :137+ while its two bound
realizations (`read_artifact/1` :25, `attribute/2` :54) sit above it, and
verifier.ex's edits land at :2178+ while its one bound realization
(`Verifier.verify/3`) sits at :17 — which is why realization_hashes.json legitimately
did not move.

Advisories (to be recorded, none blocking):

A1. ELEVENTH FALSE CLAIM. .spec/AGENTS.md:35-38 "presetting it to the empty string
    defeats both" is false for scripts/check_specs.sh, whose `:-` re-arms on an
    empty value (scripts/check_specs.sh:15). Only `make check` is defeated. The
    correct version is already on this ticket in the DELTA VERIFY of
    2026-07-27T01:26:27Z. Two-word fix.

A2. verifier.ex:2402-2412 still records "none is reachable from a test" as settled
    fact. The round-2 audit's counterexample stands unaddressed: the capture
    basename's LENGTH is predictable at test time and the artifact path is exactly
    14 bytes longer, so a sufficiently deep capture directory makes the log write
    succeed and the artifact write fail with :enametoolong. Grotesque and
    OS-dependent; I am not asking for the test. The replacement fixed the advisory
    it was aimed at but inherited this one — "no test we could find" would be true
    where "none is reachable" is not.

A3. The follow-up ticket recommended by audit round 2 — trim
    specled.tagged_tests.failed_run_preserves_attribution_artifact's structural
    clause ("not a parallel one of its own... One guard, one contract, one proof")
    to its observable content, already tested at :2215 and :2269 — has NOT been
    created. It should be, before this ticket closes.

A4. Bare `mix spec.check` has not been run at HEAD e21dfe8e, and no verifier record
    covers the merge at all. Everything td7 is provably unchanged across it, so I do
    not need one — but the merge gate must actually run bare spec.check rather than
    assume, since main's 0.9.6 lib changes (temp_name.ex, hash_store.ex, review/*)
    came in unexercised by any td7 record.

A5. Carried forward, unchanged: `dirty_provenance(nil)` ("git_dirty: unavailable" —
    HEAD resolves but `git status` fails) is still unreached by any test. Defensive
    code, not an uncovered `must` clause. Leave it.

A6. For the record, since this ticket's whole subject is tree-skew: the round-3
    briefing's premise in item (d) — "the merge touched both verifier_test.exs and
    test_helper.exs" — is itself wrong. `git diff c9b8fea1..e21dfe8e` lists 27 files
    and neither is among them. The re-measurement was therefore unnecessary rather
    than merely confirmatory. It was cheap and it came out right, so nothing is
    wrong with the tree; but a re-measurement justified by a false premise is the
    same shape as the errors this ticket keeps catching.

A7. The standing observation from round 2 holds and is now eleven for eleven: the
    CODE has survived every mutation across three verification rounds unchanged,
    while every independent read of the PROSE has found a defect — including, this
    round, a defect inside a fix for a prose defect. The diff-text sweep should be a
    permanent gate step on doc-shaped commits in this repo, not a per-round
    remediation. That is the durable finding here, and it is worth a ticket.
